One deal, two documents

A deal is a document, and its id is the sha256 of that document. The lottery's deals exist in two forms: a v1 template (the shape the raise path has always used, hashed the way PHP's json_encode happened to serialise it) and a v2 policy (the shape the signers verify — six named sections, hashed with RFC 8785). Same deal, two documents, so two different ids.

This page runs the converter in your browser. Paste a v1 template, or load one of klotto's, and it produces the v2 policy — then hashes it and tells you whether that hash is the one klotto already publishes. If it is, the conversion is not "close": it is byte-for-byte the policy the signers run.

What changed on the way across

    The six sections

    Why the id changes, and why that is the point

    A signer's authority is a list of dealIds. It refuses a transaction whose template does not hash to a listed id — that is the whole trust model, and it is why the id must be the hash of exactly the document, not of "the deal in spirit". Convert a v1 template and you get a new document, so a new id; a signer that lists the v1 id does not sign the v2 raise, and vice versa. That is not a bug in the converter. It is the reason a signer config lists both versions of a deal until the raise side has moved (the BR claims that expired on 17 September were exactly this mismatch).

    v1 templatev2 policy
    hashsha256 of PHP's json_encode output: every / escaped, every non-ASCII character as \uXXXX, keys in the order the producer wrote them. An accident, kept so 1,865 existing deals keep verifying.sha256 of RFC 8785 JCS: keys sorted, no whitespace, ECMAScript number formatting. Any implementation in any language reaches the same bytes.
    readsapi: full URLs with {name} holes and a #path the PHP walked. A template names the host it reads from.observe: a registry name (hedera.mirror), a path and a JMESPath select. The verifier decides which host that name is.
    rulesconditions: PCRE regexes with named captures, range comparisons, timelock, mathFormula — a dialect of PHP scripts.derive (JMESPath or JSONLogic) then require (JSONLogic booleans, each with a reason). The draw's digit is one op, digitAfterPoint.
    inputsEverything the raiser sent in user_parameters — its inputs and the values it resolved.Only what inputs declares, typed. Everything else is re-observed from the chain; a supplied value is never trusted.
    amountsStrings like -{ticket_price}*{PAYOUT_MULTIPLIER}, evaluated at replay and rounded to 8 places.Integers in smallest units, by construction; a non-integer result is a refusal, not a rounding.
    How this is tested

    The converter is kea/tools/convert.cjs in hbarlive_hts, a CommonJS module with a CLI; this page loads the same code bundled for a browser. Its acceptance test, qa/klotto/convert-tests.js, converts every v1 deal in the vendored klotto catalogue and asserts that the result hashes to the v2 twin klotto already publishes — eight testnet pairs, hash for hash — and that the three hand-written 2024 mainnet unlocks are refused with a named reason rather than guessed at. It never produces a policy quietly: a template it does not understand is an error, because a policy that means something other than the template would be signed by a machine that trusts the hash.

    DEAL-CONVERT1, 18 Sep 2026. Nothing here talks to a signer or a pool: the page fetches published deal documents (optionally) and computes hashes. The published catalogue is klotto.kpay.uk/deals/index.json.
